# **Modernizing Violent Action Detection with Next-Generation Spatio-Temporal Backbones and Manifold-Aware OOD Detection**

The conventional pipeline combining Spatio-Temporal Graph Convolutional Networks (ST-GCN), empirical Mahalanobis distance, and unnormalized Euclidean deep ![][image1]\-Nearest Neighbors (![][image1]\-NN) represents an obsolete foundation that is structurally ill-suited for open-world violent action surveillance. ST-GCN operates on a fixed, handcrafted graph topology defined exclusively by intra-body anthropometric connectivity1. In violent physical encounters—such as strikes, grappling, shoving, and weapon deployment—the primary discriminative indicators are dynamic cross-body interactions between distinct human actors. Because ST-GCN cannot natively create dynamic interpersonal edges without exploding parameter counts or ingesting tracking noise, its feature representations degrade precisely when ambiguity is highest2. Compounding this failure, parametric Mahalanobis distance collapses in high-dimensional latent spaces due to ill-conditioned covariance inversion and background feature dominance, while unnormalized Euclidean ![][image1]\-NN suffers from norm distortion and distance concentration, generating excessive false alarms on benign, unseen human movements4.

To achieve robust real-time violent action detection, the underlying spatio-temporal modeling backbone must transition to either **PoseConv3D (PoseC3D)** for centralized multi-person video streams or **CTR-GCN (Channel-wise Topology Refinement GCN)** for compute-constrained edge processing6. For transformer-based pipelines, **SkateFormer** provides skeletal-temporal partitioned self-attention with superior global representational capacity9. PoseConv3D eliminates graph topological fragility by converting pose sequences into 3D heatmap volumes, allowing standard 3D convolutional networks to model complex interpersonal collisions, occlusions, and variable actor counts with uniform computational complexity and state-of-the-art accuracy8.

On the out-of-distribution (OOD) detection front, unnormalized Euclidean distance must be replaced with unit-hyperspherical projection (![][image2]) using Cosine distance, which removes activation magnitude distortions and stabilizes metric neighborhoods13. Simultaneously, empirical Mahalanobis distance should be upgraded to **Virtual-logit Matching (ViM)**, which decouples in-distribution classification logits from an explicit feature null-space residual, or post-hoc **Activation Shaping (ASH)** paired with Free Energy scoring15. For specialized motion pipelines where model retraining is feasible, the **Skeleton-OOD** framework establishes explicit hyperspherical decision margins via end-to-end latent boundary optimization, delivering dependable discrimination between violent combat, routine activities, and novel non-violent anomalies18.

## **Architectural Evolution and Spatio-Temporal Backbone Replacements**

ST-GCN relies on a static adjacency matrix ![][image3] derived from biological skeletal joints1. This formulation creates severe operational bottlenecks in surveillance environments. In violent altercations, interactions are fundamentally non-physical within a single skeleton and inter-physical across multiple skeletons21. ST-GCN processes joints as isolated coordinate tuples ![][image4] across temporal sequences, making the network acutely sensitive to joint localization noise, rapid coordinate jitter, and tracking identity swaps caused by limb crossings or sudden physical impacts3. When multiple individuals grapple, coordinate-based graph convolutions struggle to distinguish which limbs belong to which identity, causing catastrophic topological distortion in the graph message-passing phase2.

Modern spatio-temporal architectures resolve these vulnerabilities through dynamic topology learning, volumetric visual representations, and partitioned attention.

### **Channel-Wise Topology Refinement (CTR-GCN)**

CTR-GCN overcomes the rigidity of static graphs by dynamically inferring channel-specific topologies for every sample7. Rather than enforcing a single globally shared adjacency matrix, CTR-GCN models spatial convolution via:

![][image5]

where ![][image6] represents the physical skeleton structure, ![][image7] is a learned global adjacency matrix, and ![][image8] is a dynamic, channel-refined correlation matrix generated via channel-wise feature differences7. This formulation allows the network to learn that upper-body velocity vectors and lower-body stability indicators correspond to distinct topological connections across individual feature channels. CTR-GCN captures subtle, asymmetric violent indicators—such as sudden defensive shielding or counter-strikes—without manual graph engineering, adding negligible computational overhead over ST-GCN and operating as an ideal drop-in replacement for edge hardware7.

### **Volumetric Skeleton Convolutions (PoseConv3D)**

PoseConv3D fundamentally rethinks skeleton-based action recognition by abandoning graph convolutions entirely6. Instead of processing raw joint coordinates, PoseConv3D rasterizes 2D or 3D keypoint trajectories into compact spatio-temporal heatmap volumes ![][image9], where ![][image10] is the number of joint types, ![][image11] is temporal depth, and ![][image12] represents spatial resolution8. Standard 3D convolutional backbones (such as SlowOnly or Res3D) are then applied directly to the volume8. This architectural paradigm provides three decisive operational advantages for violent action detection:

> 1. **Seamless Multi-Person Aggregation:** Heatmaps for an arbitrary number of interacting individuals are accumulated onto the same coordinate volume without increasing channel dimensions or computational complexity8. Cross-body physical contacts and striking trajectories are naturally captured through standard 3D convolutional receptive fields8.  
> 2. **Occlusion Robustness:** Convolutions operating on continuous heatmap distributions exhibit high robustness to missing keypoints, tracking loss, and localization noise, which typically disrupt graph adjacency calculations3.  
> 3. **Smooth Latent Manifolds:** The inductive bias of 3D CNNs produces well-regularized, continuous penultimate feature spaces that avoid the erratic clustering behaviors common to graph neural networks, directly improving downstream distance-based OOD detection11.

### **Skeletal-Temporal Transformers (SkateFormer)**

SkateFormer represents the modern vision transformer approach to human motion analysis9. Standard spatio-temporal transformers experience quadratic complexity ![][image13] when applying self-attention across all joints and frames simultaneously9. SkateFormer resolves this via its Skeletal-Temporal Multi-Head Self-Attention (Skate-MSA), which partitions joints into biomechanically coherent groups and temporal windows9. By computing attention across macro-displacements and fine-grained joint trajectories separately, SkateFormer captures long-range interpersonal dependencies across prolonged confrontation sequences while maintaining computational tractability and leading benchmark accuracy10.

## **Mathematical Breakdown and Failure Modes of Legacy OOD Detection**

The high false-alarm rates experienced in practical surveillance deployments trace directly to theoretical and numerical failure modes within parametric Mahalanobis distance and unnormalized Euclidean deep nearest-neighbor search4.

### **Covariance Degeneracy and Background Dominance in Mahalanobis Distance**

The parametric Mahalanobis distance models penultimate features ![][image14] as class-conditional Gaussian distributions with a shared covariance matrix ![][image15]:

![][image16]

The corresponding anomaly score evaluates the minimum quadratic distance to any class centroid ![][image17]:

![][image18]

In deep neural architectures trained on human motion, this formulation exhibits severe structural pathologies:

> 1. **Covariance Singularity in High Dimensions:** Penultimate embedding dimensions ![][image19] typically range from 256 to 2048\. When regularized via weight decay and non-linear activations (ReLU/GELU), features compress into lower-dimensional manifolds27. The empirical covariance matrix ![][image20] becomes ill-conditioned, with near-zero eigenvalues. Inverting ![][image15] amplifies numerical noise along off-manifold directions, producing unstable distance calculations27.  
> 2. **Class-Agnostic Background Dominance:** The leading eigenvectors of the shared covariance matrix ![][image15] do not align with action-specific semantic features; instead, they capture dominant, non-discriminative background variations, such as static standing postures, skeletal scale variance, and camera perspectives5. When an out-of-distribution motion sample arrives (such as an individual stumbling, stretching, or performing aerobic exercises), its strong background activation aligns with these dominant eigenvalues. Consequently, its projection along these non-informative components dominates the quadratic form, causing the anomaly to appear deceptively close to an in-distribution class centroid—a condition known as near-OOD blindness5.  
> 3. **Geometric Mismatch with Softmax Cones:** Deep models trained with cross-entropy loss do not form Gaussian ellipsoids in latent space. Instead, they organize features into acute, conical wedges radiating outward from the coordinate origin29. Superimposing an elliptical Gaussian distance metric onto conical manifold geometries induces systematic classification errors near decision boundaries29.

### **Distance Concentration and Norm Distortion in Euclidean Deep k-NN**

Deep ![][image1]\-NN identifies an input ![][image21] as an anomaly if its Euclidean distance to its ![][image1]\-th nearest neighbor in a cached training bank ![][image22] exceeds a threshold:

![][image23]

This formulation breaks down in deep spatio-temporal feature spaces due to two primary effects:

> 1. **Distance Concentration:** As the latent dimension ![][image19] scales, the distance distribution of independent feature components concentrates sharply:  
>    ![][image24]  
>    The metric contrast between genuine in-distribution samples and boundary OOD anomalies diminishes, degrading the Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic (AUROC)4.  
> 2. **Feature Norm Bias:** Cross-entropy training encourages the network to minimize loss by scaling up the feature norm ![][image25], as larger magnitudes directly increase logit scale and sharpen softmax probabilities13. Consequently, highly typical in-distribution actions develop large feature norms, whereas ambiguous violent interactions or novel OOD actions produce erratic, unpredictable magnitudes. In unnormalized Euclidean space, two vectors pointing in opposite semantic directions can register a small Euclidean distance if both possess small norms, while two semantically identical actions with differing magnitudes register large Euclidean distances13. This decoupling of distance from semantic orientation corrupts nearest-neighbor retrieval14.

## **Manifold-Aware Geometries via Hyperspherical Normalization and Cosine Metrics**

To resolve the distortions introduced by unconstrained vector norms and distance concentration, the penultimate feature representation must be projected onto a constrained metric manifold. Mapping latent vectors onto the unit hypersphere ![][image2] via ![][image26] normalization provides the mathematical foundation for modern distance-based OOD detection13.

For any latent representation ![][image14], the hyperspherical projection is defined as:

![][image27]

The Cosine distance between two normalized representations ![][image28] relates directly to their squared Euclidean distance:

![][image29]

![][image30]

This algebraic identity establishes that executing a Euclidean nearest-neighbor search across ![][image26]\-normalized embeddings is mathematically identical to computing a monotonic linear transformation of Cosine distance. This mapping delivers two primary operational advantages:

> 1. **Magnitude Invariance:** Projecting onto ![][image2] completely eliminates activation magnitude from the metric evaluation. The OOD decision boundary depends exclusively on the angular orientation of the action embedding, preventing overconfident, large-magnitude anomalies from masquerading as familiar in-distribution actions14.  
> 2. **Metric Regularity:** When paired with angular margin or contrastive loss objectives, in-distribution classes form compact, spherical caps distributed uniformly across the hypersphere29. Anomalous movements (such as uncoordinated falls, dancing, or equipment manipulation) map naturally into the low-density angular voids separating these clusters29.

In a hyperspherical deep ![][image1]\-NN implementation, the in-distribution reference store ![][image31] caches normalized embeddings from the training dataset:

![][image32]

For an incoming query clip with normalized embedding ![][image33], the anomaly score corresponds to the ![][image1]\-th smallest Cosine distance (or equivalently, the ![][image1]\-th largest inner product) within ![][image31]:

![][image34]

Because all embeddings reside on ![][image2], searching the reference store reduces to dense matrix-vector inner products (![][image35]). This operation can be executed in sub-millisecond latencies using hardware-accelerated tensor cores or vectorized libraries (such as Faiss)4.

## **Modern High-Performance OOD Detection Frameworks**

Beyond geometric metric normalization, modern OOD detection literature provides four advanced frameworks that consistently outperform legacy baselines on standardized benchmarks: subspace residual matching, background density regularization, dynamic activation shaping, and kinematic boundary learning.

### **Virtual-Logit Matching (ViM)**

Virtual-logit Matching (Wang et al., CVPR 2022\) combines feature space geometry with classification logits into a unified statistical test15. ViM observes that deep models embed in-distribution training data primarily within a low-dimensional affine principal subspace ![][image36], whereas OOD inputs project significant energy into the orthogonal complement, or residual null space ![][image37]15.

The feature space is decomposed using Principal Component Analysis (PCA) on centered training embeddings ![][image38]. Let ![][image39] denote the principal projection matrix formed by the top ![][image40] eigenvectors of the covariance matrix, and let ![][image41] span the residual null space ![][image37]27.

For any query embedding ![][image21], its projection into the residual null space is:

![][image42]

ViM assigns a "virtual logit" to quantify the probability of the sample originating from an unseen, unmodeled semantic category:

![][image43]

where ![][image44] is a scaling factor calculated to align the average virtual logit with the maximum in-distribution logits over a validation set. The final ViM OOD indicator integrates the virtual logit into the standard classification logits ![][image45]:

![][image46]

When an OOD motion sequence enters the network, its high residual energy in the null space causes ![][image47] to spike, sharply decreasing ![][image48]15. Across OpenOOD visual benchmarks, ViM reduces the False Positive Rate at 95% True Positive Rate (FPR95) by 10% to 20% compared to empirical Mahalanobis distance39.

### **Relative Mahalanobis Distance (RMD)**

To preserve the parametric benefits of covariance modeling while resolving background feature dominance, Relative Mahalanobis Distance (Ren et al., NeurIPS) introduces a class-agnostic background distribution ![][image49] fitted to the pooled training features across all classes5.

The RMD metric evaluates the likelihood ratio between the class-conditional density and the global background density:

![][image50]

Subtracting the background quadratic form ![][image51] penalizes features shared broadly across the training distribution (such as universal camera perspective or static body frames)5. This subtraction isolates class-discriminative signals, restoring near-OOD sensitivity without requiring iterative optimization5.

### **Activation Shaping (ASH) and Rectification (ReAct)**

Unlike distance-based methods that operate on final embeddings, activation shaping modifies intermediate activations immediately prior to the linear classification head16.

Out-of-distribution inputs frequently induce erratic, disproportionately large activations in a small subset of hidden units, artificially inflating downstream softmax confidence17.

* **ReAct** clamps activations above a static threshold ![][image52]: ![][image53].  
* **ASH (Activation Shaping)** applies dynamic percentile pruning16. For a penultimate activation vector ![][image54], ASH retains only the top ![][image55]\-th percentile of activations (typically ![][image56]) and zeroes or scales the remainder42.

Under the ASH-S variant:

![][image57]

![][image58]

Passing the shaped representation ![][image59] into the linear head produces calibrated logits ![][image60]. When evaluated via the Free Energy function:

![][image61]

ASH achieves state-of-the-art OOD separation without requiring external reference storage, matrix inversions, or training modifications16.

### **Kinematic Boundary Learning (Skeleton-OOD)**

The **Skeleton-OOD** framework (Xu et al., Neurocomputing 2024\) specifically addresses continuous spatio-temporal human action dynamics18. Conventional post-hoc OOD detectors treat spatio-temporal embeddings as static visual vectors, neglecting the sequential physical constraints of human joint trajectories18.

Skeleton-OOD resolves this via end-to-end training that incorporates:

> 1. **Latent Space Boundary Optimization:** An auxiliary objective that forces in-distribution action representations into dense, bounded hyperspherical clusters while actively synthesizing boundary pseudo-OOD samples in the latent space to establish sharp decision margins19.  
> 2. **Energy-Constrained Spatio-Temporal Regularization:** A joint loss combining cross-entropy with a statistical Kolmogorov-Smirnov test and energy-based constraints over temporal joint displacements, explicitly suppressing confident predictions on physically uncharacteristic motion sequences19.

## **Recommended Architecture and Deployment Pipelines**

To operationalize these advancements, system architectures must balance hardware compute budgets against the physical complexity of the surveillance environment. Two concrete pipelines delineate the recommended implementation paths for edge-constrained devices and enterprise surveillance servers.

### **Pipeline 1: Edge-Optimized Autonomous Surveillance**

Designed for NVIDIA Jetson Orin or embedded processing units handling local camera feeds under strict power and compute constraints.

The pipeline ingests raw 1080p video at 15 to 30 FPS through an ultra-lightweight 2D pose estimation engine (such as RTMPose-s or YOLOv8n-pose), extracting 17 keypoints per subject. The resulting coordinate sequence is fed into **CTR-GCN** using a sliding window of 32 or 64 frames. CTR-GCN dynamically refines channel-wise topologies, extracting a 256-dimensional penultimate embedding ![][image21].

OOD scoring executes directly via post-hoc **Activation Shaping (ASH-S)**. Activations below the 90th percentile are pruned, and the remaining activations are scaled before reaching the linear classification layer. An **Energy Score** evaluator then assesses the output logits. For ambiguous boundary cases, the system queries an in-memory, quantized Faiss index containing ![][image26]\-normalized training embeddings via **Hyperspherical ![][image1]\-NN (![][image71])** using Cosine distance to verify whether the movement pattern resides on the known in-distribution manifold. The total end-to-end model execution budget remains **under 15 ms per clip**, enabling deterministic real-time processing on edge hardware.

| Stage | Input Data Structure | Operational Mechanism | Output Data Structure | Latency Budget |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **1\. Pose Extraction** | Video Frames (![][image72]) | Lightweight 2D Pose Estimation (RTMPose-s) | Joint Coordinates (![][image73]) | \~5.0 ms |
| **2\. Feature Modeling** | Joint Coordinates (![][image73]) | CTR-GCN Dynamic Channel Convolutions | Latent Vector ![][image74] | \~4.5 ms |
| **3\. Activation Shaping** | Latent Vector ![][image74] | ASH-S Pruning (![][image75]) \+ Energy Score | Calibrated Logits ![][image60] | \~0.5 ms |
| **4\. Manifold Verification** | Normalized Vector ![][image76] | Hyperspherical Cosine ![][image1]\-NN via Faiss | Anomaly Score ![][image77] | \~1.5 ms |
| **5\. Threat Decision** | Calibrated Logits \+ Anomaly Score | Threshold Gating (OOD vs In-Distribution) | Alert / Normal / OOD Status | \< 0.1 ms |

### **Pipeline 2: Server-Grade Dense Multi-Person Combat Analysis**

Designed for centralized data center environments processing high-density video streams where violent altercations involve multi-person brawls, grappling, and severe visual occlusions.

The pipeline employs a high-precision multi-person pose estimator, projecting joint detections onto a multi-channel 3D heatmap volume of dimension ![][image78] (e.g., ![][image79]). This volume is processed by **PoseConv3D** using a SlowOnly-ResNet3D backbone. By accumulating all tracked actors onto a shared spatial volume, the model captures complex interpersonal striking and grappling actions without requiring explicit cross-person graph edge tracking.

OOD detection is handled via **Virtual-logit Matching (ViM)**. During offline calibration, penultimate embeddings (![][image80]) from the training set are centered to compute the global mean ![][image81], and PCA extracts the top ![][image82] principal components to construct the projection matrix ![][image83]. At runtime, the model evaluates both the classification logits and the null-space residual ![][image84] to derive the virtual logit ![][image85].

If the resulting ViM score ![][image86] falls below the operational threshold ![][image87], the clip is flagged as an unknown motion anomaly (such as a medical seizure, fainting fall, or non-violent athletic movement) and bypasses the violence classifier. If ![][image88], the clip is confirmed as an in-distribution human action, and the classification head evaluates specific violent categories (e.g., assault, battery, weapon engagement). The total server-side inference budget operates at **25 to 35 ms per multi-person clip** on modern GPU hardware.

| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |

| **2\. Volumetric Backbone** | Heatmap Volume | PoseConv3D (SlowOnly-ResNet3D) | Latent Vector ![][image89] | \~14.0 ms |
| **3\. Subspace Projection** | Latent Vector ![][image89] | Null-Space Extraction via ![][image90] | Residual Vector ![][image91] | \~1.0 ms |
| **4\. ViM Score Fusion** | Class Logits \+ Residual Vector | Virtual Logit Matching: ![][image85] | Unified Score ![][image86] | \~0.5 ms |
| **5\. Hierarchical Gating** | Unified Score ![][image86] | Conditional Gating: OOD Flag vs Threat Eval | Threat Alert or Anomaly Dispatch | \< 0.1 ms |

Upgrading from ST-GCN, empirical Mahalanobis distance, and Euclidean deep ![][image1]\-NN to modern volumetric or channel-refined backbones paired with subspace and manifold-aware OOD detectors transforms violent action detection from an experimental baseline into an industrial-grade surveillance architecture. Transitioning the spatio-temporal representation to PoseConv3D or CTR-GCN resolves the fundamental topological failures of fixed kinematic graphs during multi-person combat, providing clean, occlusion-robust feature embeddings. Simultaneously, replacing unnormalized Euclidean metrics and ill-conditioned covariance inversions with hyperspherical cosine normalization, activation shaping, and virtual-logit matching establishes mathematically rigorous decision boundaries around the in-distribution action manifold. This combined architectural overhaul suppresses false alarm rates, ensures numerical stability in high-dimensional feature spaces, and maintains dependable discrimination between routine human behaviors, novel motion anomalies, and genuine physical violence.
